hunt.justification: SCKit is an aggressive worm specifically designed to hijack remote management sessions. A successful infection compromises the organization's primary IT management channel, allowing an attacker to push malicious code across the entire fleet via the technician's workstation.

series.title: SCKit Worm Installs Rogue ScreenConnect Clients and Session Cookie Relays Across Hundreds of Endpoints

related.reason: This hunt focuses on the endpoint hijack; the subsequent lateral propagation through stolen session cookies is covered in the next hunt in this series.

meta.analysis: A single detection rule would fire on the TrapWatch task name, but SCKit rotates its indicators. This hunt uses a phased approach, correlating the presence of ScreenConnect with loader behaviour and high-frequency persistence, providing the context an analyst needs to distinguish a malicious hijack from a technician's legitimate automation.

stages.name: RMM+ Extension Authentication Bypass
observables: POST requests to ScreenConnect servers with blank RMMPlus.AccessKey

scenario.summary: Attackers exploit an authentication flaw in the third-party RMM+ extension for ScreenConnect to push commands to managed endpoints. The resulting SCKit worm establishes persistence via high-frequency scheduled tasks and registry keys, hijacks legitimate client connections, and steals technician session cookies to propagate laterally through the ScreenConnect shared toolbox.

meta.rationale: Target hosts where ScreenConnect is installed. If the software inventory is large, prioritize servers and workstations belonging to IT technicians, as they are the primary conduits for SCKit's lateral propagation.
meta.hypothesis: An intruder has exploited vulnerable ScreenConnect extensions to deploy the SCKit toolkit, which hijacks legitimate management sessions through aggressive scheduled tasks and registry persistence.

hunt.name: SCKit Endpoint Hijacking and Persistence
hunt.description: An adversary exploits vulnerable ScreenConnect extensions to deploy the SCKit toolkit, which hijacks legitimate management sessions through aggressive scheduled tasks and registry persistence. This hunt identifies the ScreenConnect estate and then searches for initial scripted loaders and C2 communication. A first agent evaluates these early infection leads. The hunt then examines high-frequency scheduled tasks and registry entries used to suppress legitimate clients. An agent synthesizes the early leads with the persistence evidence to confirm if a host has been successfully hijacked and is being used for further propagation. Finally, an analyst confirms the findings and isolates the affected endpoints.

config.content: SELECT device_hostname, package_name, package_version, vendor_name FROM hb_software_inventory WHERE LOWER(package_name) LIKE '%screenconnect%'
config.description: Identify hosts running ScreenConnect that are potentially vulnerable to the RMM+ extension exploit.
config.expected_signal: A list of hosts running ScreenConnect. Silence means the software inventory is either not collected or the product is absent.

primitive_config.label: Scope ScreenConnect hosts
primitive_config.content: SELECT device_hostname, package_name, package_version, vendor_name FROM hb_software_inventory WHERE LOWER(package_name) LIKE '%screenconnect%'
primitive_config.expected: A list of hosts running ScreenConnect. Silence means the software inventory is either not collected or the product is absent.

config.content: SELECT device_hostname, process_name, process_cmd_line, user_name, time FROM hb_process_activity WHERE (LOWER(process_cmd_line) LIKE '%eadf.php%' OR LOWER(process_cmd_line) LIKE '%sckit%' OR instr(',' || '{{loader_indicators}}' || ',', ',' || LOWER(process_name) || ',') > 0) AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days') AND ('{{scope_hosts}}' = '' OR instr(',' || '{{scope_hosts}}' || ',', ',' || device_hostname || ',') > 0)
config.description: Find executions of the Stage0Loader or subsequent stagers through command-line analysis.
config.expected_signal: PowerShell or CMD lines fetching payloads from the mo7sen.dev domain or running the named loader scripts.

primitive_config.label: Loader process activity
primitive_config.content: SELECT device_hostname, process_name, process_cmd_line, user_name, time FROM hb_process_activity WHERE (LOWER(process_cmd_line) LIKE '%eadf.php%' OR LOWER(process_cmd_line) LIKE '%sckit%' OR instr(',' || '{{loader_indicators}}' || ',', ',' || LOWER(process_name) || ',') > 0) AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days') AND ('{{scope_hosts}}' = '' OR instr(',' || '{{scope_hosts}}' || ',', ',' || device_hostname || ',') > 0)
primitive_config.expected: PowerShell or CMD lines fetching payloads from the mo7sen.dev domain or running the named loader scripts.

config.content: SELECT device_hostname, query_hostname, COUNT(*) AS lookups, MIN(time) AS first_seen FROM hb_dns_activity WHERE instr(',' || '{{c2_domains}}' || ',', ',' || LOWER(query_hostname) || ',') > 0 AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days') AND ('{{scope_hosts}}' = '' OR instr(',' || '{{scope_hosts}}' || ',', ',' || device_hostname || ',') > 0) GROUP BY device_hostname, query_hostname
config.description: Corroborate process leads by checking for host resolutions to the attacker infrastructure.
config.expected_signal: Any resolution of the named domains. Silence means the domains have rotated or no communication occurred within the lookback.

config.objective: Identify hosts where the combination of loader process activity and C2 DNS resolution indicates an active SCKit infection.
config.description: Assess whether the initial infection leads are substantive enough to warrant deep persistence hunting.
config.expected_signal: A list of hosts showing strong signs of SCKit stager execution.
config.success_criteria: A per-host verdict on early-stage infection, citing command lines and domains.

config.content: SELECT device_hostname, job_name, job_cmd_line, job_user_name, time FROM hb_scheduled_job WHERE (LOWER(job_name) = 'trapwatch' OR LOWER(job_cmd_line) LIKE '%trapwatch.ps1%') AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days') AND ('{{scope_hosts}}' = '' OR instr(',' || '{{scope_hosts}}' || ',', ',' || device_hostname || ',') > 0)
config.description: Find the high-frequency TrapWatch task that hijacks the ScreenConnect relay slot every 10 seconds.
config.expected_signal: A task named TrapWatch running as SYSTEM. Prevalence should be low (rare) across the fleet.

config.objective: Incorporate the early infection verdict with the persistence mechanisms found. Determine if the host is actively hijacked by SCKit.

config.success_criteria: A final verdict of malicious | suspicious | benign per host, citing the full infection-to-hijack chain.

config.question: the follow-on-triage verdict is malicious for at least one host

config.description: Direct the response based on the agent's synthesized verdict.
Stop the worm's local activity and prevent further session hijacking by isolating the host.
config.instructions: Isolate the host from the network immediately. Do not kill the ScreenConnect processes until memory captures are performed, as SCKit may be residing in the legitimate process context.

config.description: Review the forensic evidence and plan for remediation.
config.instructions: Examine the ProgramData\RelayTrap directory. Review the Task Scheduler for any tasks created in the last 48 hours. Confirm if the host's ScreenConnect client was actively suppressed.

config.description: Document results and close the hunt.
config.instructions: Record the total number of infected and isolated hosts. Update the detection rule candidate 'loader-process-activity' with any new filenames discovered.
